title: Terrain-Aware Flood Risk Simulation
oneLiner: Interactive flood simulator for a real Chennai neighborhood, on real terrain and rainfall data.
problem: Rigorous flood models (HEC-RAS 2D) take hours per run inside desktop GIS tools, and hazard maps only answer one static question, so nobody can ask 'what if it rains 250mm tomorrow?' and get an answer in under a second.
approach: A simplified terrain-based fill-and-spill hydraulic proxy runs over a real SRTM DEM and IMD rainfall record for Velachery, with precomputed scenario rasters blended client-side, architected so a real HEC-RAS 2D engine can later replace the proxy without touching the rest of the pipeline.

impact.label: Depression capacity filled at 2015 rainfall peak
impact.note: measured: 11.37 of 11.87 Mm³ terrain storage consumed by the actual Dec 2015 350mm event, used as a plausibility check rather than an extent validation

impact.label: What-if query latency
impact.note: measured via precomputed rasters + per-cell interpolation, e.g. 0.09 ms for a 125mm interpolated query

impact.label: Zone flooded, extreme scenario (250mm)
impact.note: proxy hydraulics output, not HEC-RAS-grade extent

impact.label: Grid resolution
impact.note: SRTM 30m DEM reprojected to EPSG:32644

honestLimit: Uses simplified proxy hydraulics, not HEC-RAS — no overland flow between depressions, no time dynamics, and no engineering-grade depth; real extent validation against 2015 imagery is deferred to the still-pending HEC-RAS track.

title: Thermal Vision-Based Airflow Optimization
oneLiner: ESP32 + thermal-camera HVAC controller, simulation-validated then confirmed working on real hardware.
problem: HVAC systems condition rooms uniformly instead of tracking where occupants actually are, wasting energy on empty space and reacting slowly to real thermal drift.
approach: A thermal camera behind a single swappable ThermalSensor interface feeds hotspot detection and a NumPy drift-forecasting model, which drives pan/tilt servo tracking and setpoint decisions over MQTT — validated first entirely in simulation, then re-verified on real AMG8833 hardware with zero logic changes.

impact.label: Simulated energy reduction
impact.note: Mean of runs, std 9.6%. Simulation vs static thermostat, not measured in a building.

impact.label: Hotspot detection F1 (AMG8833)
impact.note: measured: precision 1.000, recall 0.536 — precision near-perfect but recall below the ~90% target stated in the project plan

impact.label: Hotspot detection F1 (MLX90640)
impact.note: measured: precision 0.997, recall 0.678, same simulated eval

impact.label: Drift model test error
impact.note: measured on held-out test set, NumPy MLP

honestLimit: Only the AMG8833 build is physically wired and hardware-confirmed (MLX90640 firmware is untested on real hardware), and measured hotspot recall/F1 fall short of the ~90% accuracy figure quoted elsewhere in the project's own docs.

title: Universal Prompts
oneLiner: Guardrail-heavy prompt templates for autonomous, honest GitHub contribution and code-review agents.
problem: Turning an LLM loose on real GitHub accounts and repositories risks spam PRs, gamed achievements, and misrepresented AI authorship if the instructions don't explicitly forbid it.
approach: Two long instruction files constrain an agent to legitimate GitHub activity only: one for account achievements (audit-only, hard 'no gaming' rules), one for finding and fixing real, independently verifiable bugs in open-source repos with strict attribution rules.

impact.label: Template files
impact.note: github-achievments.txt (278 lines) + open-source_code_review.txt (596 lines)

impact.label: Explicit guardrails
impact.value: hard rule lists banning spam PRs/issues and AI co-authorship
impact.note: stated directly in both files

honestLimit: These are instruction/prompt files, not executable software — there are no automated tests or measured outcomes tracked in the files themselves.

title: AquaNexus
oneLiner: A river habitat model that measures, and reports, exactly how far it can be trusted on a river it never saw.
problem: River-habitat models are usually reported as a single accuracy score with no honest account of where they stop working, and errors found after publication are usually quietly fixed rather than disclosed.
approach: Bathymetric point clouds feed HEC-RAS hydraulics, which feed two trained models (real dissolved-oxygen labels and synthetic habitat-index labels) behind an explainable API and dashboard, then the finished model — unchanged — is scored against a second river held out from day one.

impact.label: Dissolved-oxygen model R2 (cross-validated)
impact.note: corrected from an originally published 0.442 after removing 4 defective cross-sections; beats a 'same as last reading' baseline (0.385 R2) by only 0.009

impact.label: Zero-shot transfer to held-out river, in-range
impact.note: measured on 129 in-range observations, vs +0.394 at home; collapses to -0.903 on 63 out-of-range observations (192 obs total, 5 stations)

impact.label: Test suite
impact.note: from README badge

title: brute32
oneLiner: ESP32-S3 wireless security research platform: WiFi/BLE attack primitives verified on real hardware.
problem: Existing ESP32 wireless-attack toolkits (esp32-wifi-penetration-tool, Marauder) couple every capability to a shared webserver blob, making individual primitives hard to verify or reuse in isolation.
approach: A from-scratch rebuild on ESP-IDF 5.3.x/ESP32-S3, restructured into independent, typed components (WiFi control, frame analysis, BLE, GPS, storage) tested one at a time over a serial console before any UI layer is added.

impact.note: Phase 1, confirmed on real hardware; PMKID capture works mechanically but is unproven against a PMKID-capable target

impact.note: deg->decimal, date/time, empty-field handling all confirmed on hardware

title: Deburger
oneLiner: VS Code extension that explains real ESLint/tsc/runtime findings in plain English, and never writes code.
problem: Most 'AI code assistants' either generate unrequested code or reimplement a weaker version of tools like ESLint that already solve the underlying analysis problem well.
approach: Calls ESLint's Linter API and the real TypeScript compiler directly for static findings, watches live debug sessions via the Debug Adapter Protocol for real runtime exceptions, and feeds both into an LLM prompt that is constrained to explain, never generate, code.

impact.label: Test suite
impact.note: 10 suites, from README's own npm test run

impact.label: Demo analysis run
impact.note: real run against the bundled demo-project

impact.label: Packaged extension
impact.note: verified working .vsix; unbundled node_modules since no bundler is configured yet

honestLimit: No bundler is configured, so the packaged .vsix ships ESLint/TypeScript/Babel unbundled — functional but larger than necessary; sidebar/panel screenshots require a live VS Code window and aren't included.

title: EasyRAS (RAS Copilot)
oneLiner: Planned COM-automation wrapper to simplify HEC-RAS's UI; currently a sourced feature catalog, no app yet.
problem: HEC-RAS's native UI spreads related settings across many disconnected editors (Geometry, Flow, 2D Areas, Structures, Plan/Run Manager), so newcomers struggle to find the right field for a given task.
approach: The plan is a COM-automation wrapper that replaces only the interaction layer, never the underlying feature set, gated on a Phase 0 rule that every UI field in the catalog must be verified against the official HEC-RAS manuals rather than recalled from memory.

impact.label: Application code
impact.note: repository currently contains only the project plan and the Phase 0 catalog — no bridge or UI implemented

honestLimit: No working software exists yet — only the project plan and a Phase 0 HEC-RAS feature catalog; the COM-automation bridge and UI described in the plan are unbuilt.

title: FloGravity
oneLiner: Hydraulically-constrained least-cost path for a gravity-fed drainage line, over any DEM.
problem: A generic hiking-trail least-cost path only avoids steep terrain, but a gravity-fed drainage channel also needs a minimum continuous downhill grade, a hard maximum grade, and a real cost for crossing an existing drainage channel head-on.
approach: A DEM-to-route pipeline (reprojection, slope/aspect, pysheds conditioning, D8 flow accumulation) feeds a custom anisotropic Dijkstra router that penalizes perpendicular channel crossings more than parallel ones, built as a scoped warm-up for a larger multi-inlet capstone (TADRO).

impact.label: Slope calculation validated
impact.value: checked against the exact analytic constant
impact.note: pytest suite, synthetic tilted-plane test

impact.label: Sample DEM tested end-to-end
impact.note: real DEM via pysheds' own sample data

impact.label: Anisotropic routing
impact.value: custom 8-connected Dijkstra with directional channel-crossing penalty
impact.note: documented as the key difference from a standard least-cost-path tutorial

honestLimit: No validation yet against a real constructed drainage line, and no multi-objective or multi-inlet network routing — both stated explicitly as stretch goals not implemented here, reserved for the TADRO capstone.

title: GnatSonic
oneLiner: Two ESP32 boards exchanging data over near-ultrasonic sound, no WiFi or Bluetooth — an air-gap covert channel demo.
problem: Air-gap covert channels — moving data between computers with no network link at all — are a documented real attack class (e.g. the MOSQUITO paper), worth understanding hands-on rather than only reading about.
approach: Phase 0 tooling only so far: ESP32 firmware plays a 15-22kHz sine sweep through an I2S DAC and speaker, and a Python script records it back, plots a spectrogram, and reports per-band SNR — gating every later phase (modem, framing, reliability) on real measured hardware data instead of assumed specs.

impact.label: Development phase
impact.note: tooling built and pushed; physical hardware validation has not happened yet, per README

impact.label: Reference prior art
impact.value: MOSQUITO covert channel (Guri et al., IEEE DSC 2018)
impact.note: cited demonstration of ultrasonic data transfer up to 9m between air-gapped PCs

impact.label: Design risk mitigation
impact.value: piezo buzzer swapped for I2S DAC + real speaker
impact.note: documented reasoning; Phase 0 exists specifically to confirm it works, not yet measured

honestLimit: No frequency band, symbol timing, or guard interval is fixed anywhere yet — every phase after Phase 0 is explicitly blocked pending real measured hardware data.

title: InsightWell
oneLiner: Turns raw airline complaint text into clustered, scored root-cause categories with no manual tagging.
problem: Support/ops teams need to know what customers are complaining about, how bad it is, and where to look first, but keyword-list tagging is manual and doesn't group complaints the way a human would.
approach: A single linear Python pipeline embeds and clusters complaints with BERTopic, scores sentiment with a RoBERTa model, aggregates volume/trend/confidence per category into one static JSON artifact, and a fully static Next.js dashboard reads that artifact with no backend.

title: LancerScape
oneLiner: On-chain milestone escrow for freelancing with hybrid human-verified dispute resolution, testnet MVP.
problem: Centralized freelance escrow platforms hold funds with opaque, algorithmic or unaccountable dispute resolution, creating a single point of failure and no visibility into how fund decisions are made.
approach: Client funds are locked in a Solidity escrow contract per milestone; a backend analyzes submitted evidence and an admin decides disputed outcomes, with the smart contract itself executing the resulting payment on Base Sepolia testnet.

title: Marine Acoustic Monitor
oneLiner: Edge-computed marine anomaly detector, simulation-validated end to end before any hardware is purchased.
problem: Monitoring marine ecosystems with human observers or connectivity-dependent systems is expensive, and a low-cost buoy or dock unit needs to flag anomalies locally without constant high-bandwidth connectivity.
approach: On-device feature extraction combines acoustic (MFCC, spectral) and environmental (temperature, pH, turbidity, salinity) signals into one joint vector, fed to an unsupervised Isolation Forest anomaly detector — proven first entirely against synthetic hardware, with real production edge software runnable today in a mock-hardware mode.

impact.label: Anomaly precision (simulated)
impact.note: Recall 0.69, F1 0.78; mean of 30 seeded runs. Synthetic anomalies vs synthetic background, no field data yet.

impact.label: Vessel-type anomaly recall
impact.note: detector isn't type-aware, so precision is diluted

impact.label: Storm/environmental anomaly detection
impact.note: root-caused: 34 acoustic vs 8 environmental dims dilutes the signal; a measured candidate fix trades overall precision 0.97->0.72 for storm recall 0.05->0.59

honestLimit: No hardware has been purchased yet — every number here is from synthetic-vs-synthetic simulation with no real field or hardware validation, per the project's own locked DECISIONS.md.

title: MedicaLog
oneLiner: Server-first medication/condition tracker with constrained, non-clinical AI pattern awareness and full data control.
problem: Health-tracking apps often over-collect data, bury users in unrequested 'insights', and give users no real way to reset, correct, or delete what's been stored.
approach: A server-first Next.js app enforces ownership and transactional writes on every mutation, logs medication/meal data deterministically, and feeds only structured, deterministic features (never raw text) to an LLM that is explicitly barred from diagnosis, urgency, or recommendations.

title: Mend
oneLiner: Offline-first Android scheduler that negotiates a realistic day with deterministic logic and an optional AI layer.
problem: A to-do list doesn't model the real shape of a day — fixed commitments, habits, and goal work competing for genuinely free time — and most schedulers either over-automate silently or don't adapt when reality changes.
approach: A pure-Kotlin engine (no Android dependency, unit-tested on the JVM) lays down fixed blocks and habits, scores pending tasks by deadline/importance/reliability, and greedily packs the remainder into free time — proposing changes rather than silently rewriting the day; an optional, narrowly-scoped Anthropic integration only turns language into one of four pre-validated constraint shapes.

impact.note: per README's Current phase section, through natural-language parsing and offline degradation

impact.label: Engine isolation
impact.value: scheduling-engine module has zero Android dependency
impact.note: pure Kotlin, testable on the JVM with no emulator, per README architecture

impact.note: deliberate floor for per-criticality notification channels and native java.time, per README

title: BERTopic Bug Fix (Open-Source Contribution)
oneLiner: Root-caused and fixed a real bug in BERTopic's find_topics for list-valued search terms, with new tests.
problem: BERTopic's find_topics wrapped a list search_term in an extra list before embedding it, so sentence-transformers' tokenizer fell through to its text-pair branch — a one-element list raised an IndexError, and a longer list silently encoded only the first two terms as a pair.
approach: Normalized search_term to a list of strings up front, averaged the resulting per-term embeddings into a single query embedding (a no-op for a single string), and added explicit errors for empty lists or non-string entries.

impact.label: Root cause identified
impact.value: sentence-transformers tokenize() text-pair fallback on nested lists
impact.note: documented in the commit message

impact.label: Tests added
impact.note: from the commit's own diffstat

impact.label: Upstream issues addressed
impact.note: referenced directly in the commit message

honestLimit: This is a single fix commit on a personal fork against upstream MaartenGr/BERTopic; whether the pull request was accepted upstream isn't recorded in this repository.

title: Snitchwatt
oneLiner: From-scratch TVLA side-channel leakage auditor, validated against simulated power traces with a real threshold.
problem: Determining whether a cryptographic device's power consumption leaks secret-dependent information usually requires lab equipment and proprietary tooling; TVLA is the published methodology real hardware-security labs use, but it needs a correctly-implemented statistical engine to trust.
approach: Implements the standard TVLA protocol — Welch's t-test per time sample between fixed and random trace groups, flagged at the published |t|>4.5 threshold — against a Hamming-weight-plus-Gaussian-noise trace simulator, with the trace source fully abstracted so a real oscilloscope capture can plug in later with zero engine changes.

impact.label: Leak stat, unprotected (flag at >4.5)
impact.note: FLAGGED. The masked implementation scores 3.34 and passes; one with a residual leak scores 4.98 and is caught.

impact.label: Masked implementation
impact.note: clean simulated countermeasure, no data-dependent component

impact.label: Masked with residual leak
impact.note: correctly detects a smaller residual leak vs the fully unprotected profiles

impact.label: TVLA threshold used
impact.note: the standard published TVLA pass/fail threshold, ~99.999% confidence

honestLimit: Runs entirely on simulated Hamming-weight power traces — no real hardware, oscilloscope, or target device has been tested; hardware integration via a ChipWhisperer-Nano is deferred, per README's own roadmap.

title: Weir
oneLiner: Admission control for overloaded human approvers: live pressure, bounded queues, agent proposals under a deterministic policy.
problem: Approval workflows (procurement, expense, access requests) treat a slow human approver as an inbox-design problem, so requests silently pile up under overload with no live signal until someone escalates.
approach: Each approver's live pressure state (Normal/Elevated/Critical) is computed from a rolling decision-latency window with hysteresis; under sustained Critical pressure, either a deterministic offline policy or a Claude-driven governance agent proposes delegation/auto-approval, but every proposal — from either mode — must pass a separate deterministic validator before it touches the ledger.

impact.label: Test suite
impact.note: policy engine plus full FastAPI request lifecycle, per README

impact.label: Pressure model
impact.note: computed from both resolved-decision latency and live queue-wait time

impact.label: Governance modes
impact.value: offline deterministic stand-in and live Claude-driven proposals
impact.note: both routed through the same policy_engine.validate_proposal before any ledger write

honestLimit: README's own roadmap lists Postgres, a Redis-backed shared state store, and real authentication/authorization as not yet built — the current state store is single-process SQLite, not production-scale.
